Granulomatous Mastitis: fibrous and lymphoid tissue infiltrated by large epithelioid granulomas

Granulomatous Lobular Mastitis: Mammography finding: 1.2 cm mass with irregular borders near axillary process of right breast
Physical examination finding: firm mass in upper outer quadrant of right breast
Granulomatous Mastitis: Frozen section of specimen: granulomatous inflammation
Microscopic examination of tumor: fibrous and lymphoid tissue infiltrated by large epithelioid granulomas with central acellular necrosis and many giant cells
Special (acid fast) stains: no microorganisms within necrosis
Sentinel lymph node: 0.9 cm in greatest diameter, same morphologic appearance as tumor
Physical examination finding: skin edema and erythema

top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient's presentation of a palpable breast lump, skin edema, and erythema, combined with the microscopic examination of the tumor showing fibrous and lymphoid tissue infiltrated by large epithelioid granulomas, central acellular necrosis, and giant cells, is highly suggestive of Granulomatous Mastitis. The absence of microorganisms within the necrosis and the sentinel lymph node involvement also support this diagnosis.

While the mammography findings and physical examination of a firm mass in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast could suggest Granulomatous Lobular Mastitis, the lack of specific findings such as granulomatous lobulitis, lobular inflammation, and epithelioid cell clusters makes this diagnosis less likely compared to Granulomatous Mastitis.

There is insufficient evidence to support the diagnosis of Idiopathic Granulomatous Mastitis, as key features such as rapid progression, recurrent episodes, painful breast mass, skin retraction, and axillary lymphadenopathy are not mentioned in the patient's presentation.
